ModelValidatorExternal.release_notes:
### Report Config Editor

- **Curve IDs Now Show Their Channel and Source.** In the PlotToCurvesMap and Metrics tabs, each CurveId is now displayed together with the channel and source it was defined with in CurvesConfig (e.g. `C1 - METER_VPU_POC_1 [PSCAD]`), both in the cell and in the selection dropdown. This makes it easy to tell which curve is which without switching back to CurvesConfig. The label is display-only: the saved configuration and exported Excel file still contain just the CurveId.

ModelValidator.release_notes:
### AI Assistant

- **New: In-App AI Assistant.** An AI Assistant window, opened from the Help panel or the Project Manager, can answer questions about Model Validator and operate the open project: setting up handlers, mapping channels, running suites, validating and reporting. It works through the app's built-in MCP server, so everything it does is visible in the app straight away.
- **You Approve Every Change.** The Assistant reads freely, but each action that changes the project or settings shows an Approve / Reject card first. Outside AI clients connect with their own access token.
- **One AI Connection for Every AI Feature.** AI Configuration now sets a single connection used by the Assistant and by the single-step AI features (config authoring, AI full check, AI channel mapping, report copilot): either an AI subscription through its command-line tool, or an API key for OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini, with a main and a fast model.
- **Help Chat Replaced by the AI Assistant.** Documentation search is now a plain keyword search over the shipped documentation, kept up to date automatically; the separate Help Chat, feedback/corrections and online documentation sync have been removed.
- **New: AI Assistant in the Project Manager.** The Assistant and AI Configuration are available from the Project Manager, and the same Assistant window carries on in the main window after a project opens.
- **New: The Assistant Follows Runs Itself.** After starting a suite run or a validation, the Assistant can ask the app to tell it when the work finishes. A live timer in the chat shows progress and elapsed time, and when the run finishes the Assistant carries on (mapping, validation, summary) without having to be told to check.

### Case and Configuration Inspectors

- **New: Case Inspectors.** PSS®E and PSCAD cases are inspected when loaded, and on demand, without running a simulator: the files the case folder holds and uses, the network topology, dynamic models (plant controllers, playback, user-defined models and their DLLs), model documentation found in the case folder, and channels. Problems are reported as checks; suggested settings, such as monitoring and Thevenin branches, come with their evidence and are only applied with your approval.
- **New: Test Suite Configuration Inspector.** Summarizes a suite's tests, operating points, events and run durations, shows which tests no validation covers, and cross-checks the suite against the loaded cases (e.g. playback tests need a playback-capable .dyr).

### AI Model Tuning (PSS®E)

- **New: AI Tunes Dynamic Model Parameters.** When validations fail, the AI can tune .dyr parameters inside a plan you approve: which parameters may change, the range of each, and at most 5 iterations. Changes within the plan run without further approval; anything outside it asks first.
- **Tunes the Suite's Corner Cases Together.** The AI picks the tests at the edges of the operating envelope (active and reactive power, POC voltage, SCR, X/R) and judges every change across all of them, reporting what each iteration fixed and what it broke. All tests on the .dyr are re-checked before a result is offered.
- **Originals Are Never Touched Until You Accept.** Tuning works on copies of every .dyr the tuned models live in (e.g. the base and the playback .dyr). Only when you accept is each original replaced, and every original is backed up first.
- **Uses Case Documentation for User-Defined Models.** For vendor models, the AI looks up parameter meanings in the documentation found in the case folder, and asks you when there is none.

### DYR Editor

- **Changed: Saving Writes Only What You Changed.** Saving in the DYR Editor previously rewrote the whole file, reordering models, dropping comments and rewriting user-defined model records. It now changes only the edited values, leaves every other line exactly as it was, and checks the file afterwards; nothing is saved if a value doesn't read back as entered. A model's bus number, name and ID can no longer be changed here.

### Benchmarking and Validation

- **Changed: Benchmarks Now Judge Trips.** A comparison where a model tripped was previously set aside as "Tripped". Now both models tripping within the time tolerance, and matching before the trip, is a Pass; only one of them tripping is a Fail, with the reason naming which one.
- **Fixed: PSS®E Placeholder Values Distorted Results and Plots.** PSS®E can write values around 1e38 at the instant a model trips. These are now replaced by interpolation wherever curves are read, so they no longer distort validation, benchmarks or plot scaling.
- **Fixed: Static Data Test Skipped PSS®E Bus Voltages.** Bus voltage channels named like `VOLT 599001 [BUS_NAME 275.00]` didn't match their static data entry (`VOLT 599001`), so the voltage Static Data Test was silently skipped. They now match.
- **New: Warning When Benchmark Results Are Out of Date.** Validation results show when each handler's result file was written, and warn when they are far apart, e.g. when one handler wasn't re-run.
- **New: Reactive Current from P/Q/V Channels.** For results without current channels (typically PSS®E), reactive current at the POC can be derived from the mapped reactive power and voltage, in per unit and in amps, so reactive current checks are no longer skipped.
- **Benchmark Comment Names the Compared Handlers.** The benchmark description now names the actual reference and comparison handlers instead of always saying PSSE and PSCAD.

### Result Viewer

- **Fixed: Curves Could Fall Outside the View.** The axis range was set by the first curve drawn (and the time range by the last), so a curve at a different level, often TSAT, could be off-screen. The axes now span every curve shown.
- **Overlapping Curves Are Distinguishable.** Each handler's curve is drawn in its own colour and line style (solid, dashed, dotted, dash-dot), so a curve lying exactly on another stays visible.
- **Fixed: Benchmark Plots Showed Extra Curves.** A benchmark plot now shows only the two handlers its result compares.
- **Fixed: Crash Opening a Test With Nothing Validated.** Opening the results of a test whose validation found no mapped channels crashed the viewer; it now shows the reason instead.

### Execution

- **Fixed: The AI Assistant Saw Running Suites as Idle.** A suite started from its own Run button or by the Assistant was reported as not running, and the Assistant couldn't stop it. It now sees and can stop every running suite however it was started.
- **Fixed: Suite Progress Counted the Wrong Tests.** A run of a subset of tests measured progress against the ticked rows rather than the tests actually started.
